rites.name: Grimougok
rites.text: Grimougok is a concept of Tarnor, the rootsong that hums through the Singing as the first world-roots condense from silence. During the Age of Sundering it was the note that split old bonds apart when landfall tore continents from their mothers.

rites.name: Osuvamari
rites.text: Osuvamari is the concept of a binding oath that holds the doors between worlds shut, sworn in the Courts during the age of divine trials. It is spoken aloud by the council whenever a new threshold is raised, and its weight is felt as a settling of the air.

rites.name: Siaranum
rites.text: Siaranum is the concept of a binding oath sworn at the council of the Courts, a vow that held the first doors between worlds shut until its terms were fulfilled. It is said to hum in the groves when a sovereign speaks a promise they cannot break.

rites.name: Ositheth
rites.text: Ositheth is the concept of the branching ending of Tarnor, the moment in the Three Futures when a single thread splits into many and the Library must shelve every outcome at once. It is less a being than a pressure felt across all three futures, pulling each possibility toward its own consequence.

rites.name: Drathouktun
rites.text: Drathouktun is the concept of the Tarnor branch-point in the Three Futures, the moment an ending splits and the Library shelves each outcome as its own volume. It is not a being that acts but a principle that keeps the futures apart so none can collapse into another.
